title: Light, renewed daily (Isaiah 45:7)
hookLine: the first blessing praises God who forms light and renews creation every day

cards: There's a verse from Isaiah that the prayer book borrows, and then quietly changes by one word. That's unusual.
The verse is God speaking through the prophet: I form the light and create darkness, I make peace and create evil. The rabbis wanted it for the first blessing before the morning Shema.
But they didn't want the word evil in a morning blessing. So they swapped it.

teach.h: I FORM THE LIGHT, AND CREATE DARKNESS.
teach.b: In the old Jewish translation, Isaiah forty-five reads: "I form the light, and create darkness; I make peace, and create evil; I am the LORD, that doeth all these things."
The morning blessing begins: blessed are you, yotzer or, who forms light and creates darkness, who makes peace and creates all things.
Evil became all. The Talmud, in tractate Berakhot, notices the change and gives a reason: it's a more graceful way to say it.
The meaning holds, because all includes everything, but the morning doesn't open with the word evil on your lips.
The blessing over daylight mentions darkness, too, and the Talmud says that's deliberate: you mention night in the day, and day at night. Then comes the line behind today's carry.
God, the blessing says, in his goodness renews every day, continually, the work of creation. Hamechadesh. Renews.
Not created once, long ago, and left running like a clock. Made new, today.
Some Hasidic teachers later pressed the idea further: if creation is renewed continually, it's renewed every moment, and nothing simply carries on by itself.
Whatever you make of that, the blessing's picture is plain. Each sunrise isn't a rerun. It's the world being given again.

how: Yotzer Or is the first of the blessings before the Shema in the morning service, said right after Barchu; on Shabbat and festivals it is expanded with additional hymns.

games.q: inside Yotzer Or — tap the pairs.
p: I form the light, and create darkness

s: the blessing quotes Isaiah word for word
it changes create evil to create all things; the Talmud calls it a more graceful phrasing.
the morning blessing over light also mentions darkness
the Talmud says to mention night in the day, and day at night.
the blessing says creation was finished once and left running
it says God renews the work of creation every day, continually.

games.q: you're composing the first blessing of the morning from Isaiah's verse: I make peace, and create evil. what do you do with the word evil?
games.why: the rabbis changed it to creates all things. the Talmud says it's a more graceful way to say it, without losing the meaning.

practice: Find the nearest light, a window, a lamp, a patch of sun on the floor, and notice its color and the edges of the shadows it makes. Imagine it didn't exist a moment ago and has just been given, new, for you to see by.
If you pray, you can say yotzer or, who forms light; if not, simply watch it.
